_readme: SAIRNlaw deadline engine seed -- US Federal civil litigation (FRCP).
This is NOT run as a migration. It is loaded through api/legal-deadlines.js's
add_rule / add_holidays actions, which reject any rule lacking an authority
URL and stamp verified_by from the real session. That way every row was put
there by someone who read the rule, and the row records who and when --
the same discipline as sc_scrubrules and sc_credential_scope in SAIRNcode.
Every day count below was read from the primary source on 2026-08-21 and is
quoted in each rule's authority.quote field. None came from memory.
ONE RULE WAS DELIBERATELY ABSENT IN PHASE 1 AND IS NOW RESOLVED:
absence, so the history is kept rather than quietly deleted:
1. Fed. R. Civ. P. 12(a)(3) -- 'within 60 days after service on the officer
or employee or service on the United States attorney, WHICHEVER IS LATER'.
A two-trigger rule. Phase 1's engine modelled one trigger per rule, so
encoding it then would have computed from whichever trigger happened to
be supplied -- too early roughly half the time, the direction that loses
a right. RESOLVED in Phase 2: the multi-trigger capability now expresses
it, and the engine REFUSES with INCOMPLETE_TRIGGERS unless both service
2. The 90-day variant of 12(a)(1)(A)(ii) (waiver request sent to a defendant
outside any judicial district) is present but flagged: it shares a trigger
event with the 60-day variant and is distinguished only by a fact about
the defendant's location that the engine has no field for. Both are
included with DISTINCT trigger_event names so the user must state which
situation applies -- the engine will never guess between them, and
overlapping windows on one trigger would correctly raise AMBIGUOUS_RULE.
SERVICE EXTENSION, applied only where it genuinely applies: Rule 6(d) adds 3
days when a party 'may or must act within a specified time AFTER BEING
SERVED'. The waiver deadlines run from when the request was SENT, not from
service, so 6(d) is not attached to them. That is a deliberate omission, not
an oversight -- attaching it would extend a deadline that the rule does not
extend.
PHASE 2 ADDITIONS (2026-08-21) -- FRAP appellate. Every value read from the
primary source and quoted. Rule 12(a)(3), omitted in Phase 1 because the
engine could not express 'whichever is later', is now BACKFILLED using the
multi-trigger capability -- closing a known documented hole rather than
leaving it open while adding new coverage.
NOTE ON FRAP 26(c) vs FRCP 6(d): these are differently SHAPED, not just
differently numbered. 6(d) is an enumerated allowlist (mail / clerk /
consented). 26(c) is a NEGATIVE condition -- 3 days are added when a paper
is NOT served electronically. The engine holds a separate predicate for
each; a single shared allowlist silently refused FRAP extensions before
this was fixed.

rules.label: Answer to a complaint after service of summons and complaint

authority.quote: within 21 days after being served with the summons and complaint

rules.label: Answer after a waiver request sent to a defendant within a judicial district

authority.quote: within 60 days after the request for a waiver was sent
authority.note: Runs from when the request was SENT, not from service, so Rule 6(d)'s 3-day service extension is not attached.

rules.label: Answer after a waiver request sent to a defendant outside any judicial district

authority.quote: or within 90 days after it was sent to the defendant outside any judicial district
authority.note: Distinct trigger_event from the 60-day variant on purpose: the engine must never guess which situation applies.

rules.label: Answer to a counterclaim or crossclaim

authority.quote: A party must serve an answer to a counterclaim or crossclaim within 21 days after being served with the pleading that states the counterclaim or crossclaim

rules.label: Answer by the United States, an agency, or an officer sued in an official capacity

authority.quote: must serve an answer to a complaint, counterclaim, or crossclaim within 60 days after service on the United States attorney

rules.label: Answer by a US officer or employee sued in an individual capacity

authority.quote: must serve an answer to a complaint, counterclaim, or crossclaim within 60 days after service on the officer or employee or service on the United States attorney, whichever is later
authority.note: BACKFILLED from Phase 1's deliberate omission. Requires the multi-trigger capability; the engine refuses unless BOTH service dates are supplied, because resolving from one would be too early whenever the other governs.

authority.quote: the notice of appeal required by Rule 3 must be filed with the district clerk within 30 days after entry of the judgment or order appealed from
authority.note: The retrigger clause implements 4(a)(4)(A): 'the time to file an appeal runs for all parties from the entry of the order disposing of the last such remaining motion.' That REPLACES the trigger -- it does not add days.

rules.label: Notice of appeal, civil case where the United States is a party

authority.quote: The notice of appeal may be filed by any party within 60 days after entry of the judgment or order appealed from if one of the parties is: (i) the United States
authority.note: Distinct trigger_event from the 30-day rule on purpose. Whether the United States is a party is a fact the engine has no field for, so the user must state which situation applies rather than the engine guessing between two overlapping rules.

rules.label: Notice of appeal by a criminal defendant

authority.quote: a defendant's notice of appeal must be filed in the district court within 14 days after the later of: (i) the entry of either the judgment or the order being appealed; or (ii) the filing of the government's notice of appeal
authority.note: The same 'later of' shape as FRCP 12(a)(3). One capability unlocked both.

rules.label: Response to an amended pleading, the later of the time remaining on the original and 14 days (Federal)

limbs.label: the time remaining to respond to the original pleading, i.e. that deadline itself
14 days after service of the amended pleading

authority.quote: Unless the court orders otherwise, any required response to an amended pleading must be made within the time remaining to respond to the original pleading or within 14 days after service of the amended pleading, whichever is later.
authority.note: NOW COMPUTABLE, AND IT IS THE ODDEST OF THE FIVE. Refused by this engine until 2026-08-24. The second limb is an ordinary 14-day period, but THE FIRST LIMB IS NOT A PERIOD AT ALL -- "the time remaining to respond to the original pleading" is the original deadline itself, already fixed by whatever rule set it. It is encoded as a ZERO-DAY period running from that deadline, which is the faithful reading: a period of no days from a date is that date. THE CONSEQUENCE, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT IS THE ENGINE'S KNOWN WEAK POINT: this row requires the caller to supply a date that is itself a DEADLINE, not an event. The engine does not compute the original response deadline and does not check that the date given is one -- it is the same trigger-derivation limit that applies across the engine, but sharper here, because every other rule at least asks for something that happened in the world. Compute the original deadline first, with the rule that governs it, and feed the result in. If the original pleading was a complaint served in the ordinary way, that is the FRCP 12(a)(1)(A)(i) row. NOT ENCODED: the opening "Unless the court orders otherwise", which is an order the engine cannot see, and Rule 15(a)(1)'s separate amend-as-of-course periods, which are already their own rows.
Observed dates. Where a holiday falls on a Saturday the preceding Friday is observed; where it falls on a Sunday the following Monday is observed.

dates.name: Birthday of Martin Luther King, Jr.

authority.note: Loaded alongside 2026 because a period triggered late in 2026 crosses into 2027, and the engine refuses on the year it actually needs rather than the year of the trigger.
